extracted.intended_audience: marketing/PR teams and tech brands (startups, consumer electronics, AI, mobility, health, smart home, and global companies) preparing press outreach for CES
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, event-specific guidance for securing national media coverage tied to CES (in-person or remote launches), covering integrated PR + paid media, awards and speaking opportunities, timing/deadlines, press kit requirements, pitching tactics, and post-show amplification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine PR + Paid Media for Maximum Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an integrated approach that combines traditional PR with paid media, content partnerships, and national broadcast placements to increase chances of coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page presents a performance-focused integration (PR + paid media + content partnerships + national broadcast placements). Examples of client gains include TV features on ABC/CBS/NBC and streaming networks, online placements on high-authority tech sites and consumer outlets, social + influencer extensions, and SEO optimization for searches like “best CES 2026 innovations.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure TV, Online, Social, and SEO Placements
rubrics_metrics.description: Target a mix of broadcast, high-authority online outlets, influencer/social extensions, and search-optimized content to maximize visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific placement targets called out: TV features on ABC/CBS/NBC and streaming networks; online placements on high-authority tech sites and consumer outlets; social and influencer extensions to boost engagement; SEO optimization for relevant searches. Aim for cross-channel amplification rather than single-channel placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Win Awards & Speaking Opportunities to Position Your Product
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursue media-curated award programs and conference speaking slots to position the product as a CES standout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tactics include submitting for Innovation Awards, targeting “Top Picks” lists from outlets like Digital Trends, Engadget, and Tom’s Guide, and applying for CES Conference Sessions to elevate thought leadership. Using awards/speaking to create editorial hooks and third-party validation is emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance-based PR guarantee (confirmed placements or qualified coverage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a performance-based PR model that requires verified results: confirmed placements or qualified media coverage, or no payment is owed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page markets a guarantee: delivery of confirmed placements or qualified media coverage, otherwise the client doesn’t pay. This sets an outcome-oriented standard for vendor performance and client expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start Media Outreach Early (timing/deadlines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin outreach well before the event because journalists finalize CES plans months in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists often confirm CES schedules by October (e.g., October 2026 for CES 2027). The page advises planning ahead and scheduling outreach early to meet journalists’ booking timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch Tech & Consumer Journalists Personally
rubrics_metrics.description: Personalize outreach by pitching individual tech and consumer journalists directly rather than relying on broad blasts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly says to 'Pitch tech & consumer journalists personally.' Implicit guidance: tailor messages to reporter beats and demonstrate why the product fits their coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit for Innovation Awards (meet award deadlines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter relevant CES/industry innovation awards to gain editorial visibility and validation; observe specific submission deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page calls out submitting for Innovation Awards and gives a sample deadline: 'Submit for CES Innovation Awards by August 29, 2026.' Treat award submission as a formal part of the PR timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare a Complete Press Kit (assets & product details)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assemble a comprehensive press kit containing high-resolution assets and detailed product information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required components listed: high-res images, demo videos, product details. The page emphasizes a 'complete press kit' as a prerequisite for effective pitching and journalist follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft Storylines Tied to Trending Themes
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame your product within current trends (e.g., AI, sustainability, smart home) to increase editorial relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended themes to tie into: AI, sustainability, smart home. The page advises crafting storylines that align with trending topics journalists are covering to create an editorial hook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend Coverage Beyond the Event (post-show amplification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan follow-up content and amplification strategies to convert one week of CES buzz into sustained visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested post-show tactics: follow-up features like 'Top Tech to Watch in 2026,' SEO-optimized press articles and backlinks, paid ad retargeting tied to CES keywords, and repurposing coverage highlights for TikTok & YouTube to maintain momentum year-round.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target National and High-Authority Outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for national media and high-authority tech and consumer outlets to maximize impact and credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists target outlets as examples of desirable coverage: CNN, Forbes, Wired, Mashable, TechCrunch, Digital Trends, Engadget, Tom’s Guide, and national broadcast networks. Use these outlets as benchmarks for desired reach and prestige.
